correctness.rationale: Equation (19) of the source becomes \(c=I_k(\beta+ku_1/(1+ku_2I_k))\). The positive root is unique. Direct differentiation gives positive \(F_I\) and \(F_k\), hence \(dI_k/dk<0\). Multiplication gives the displayed quadratic, whose positive root yields the three asymptotic regimes by the sign of \(u_1-cu_2\). The claim is explicitly restricted to equilibrium algebra, so no unsupported stability inference is made.

value.rationale: The source stresses that information parameters do not affect \(\mathcal R_0\), which leaves open how strongly they can change endemic burden. The theorem gives an exact answer: a natural saturation threshold separates asymptotic suppression from a positive floor, with a critical square-root slowdown. This is a structural property of the model parameters and not an arbitrary numerical slice.
